basis: Thymic immunodeficiency, congenital heart defects and parathyroid deficiency define it; intellectual disability 72/78. Scoliosis 37/78 omitted under cap.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss, present in 20/20 reported patients.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; respiratory distress in 3/6 does not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Pigmentation disorder localized to the eyelids, which belong to the ocular axis.
Inherited episodic dystonia is a neurologic movement disorder; muscle contractions do not establish primary muscle disease.
Inherited sphingolipid biosynthesis defect; no common additional organ damage established for this umbrella concept.
Epilepsy syndrome defined by neonatal or infantile seizures with predictable spontaneous remission.
Immune-mediated inflammation and demyelination of peripheral nerves and roots; weakness reflects nerve injury rather than direct muscle disease.
Lysosomal lipid disorder; neurodegeneration in most, hepatic storage 7/13, splenic infiltration 4/13 and marrow histiocytosis 4/4.
Colonic adenomatous polyposis and a primary CNS tumor define this syndrome; pigmented fundus lesions do not establish ocular dysfunction.
Degeneration of the peripheral retina.
EBV-driven B-cell lymphoproliferation with pulmonary infiltration; CNS lesions occur in roughly 30-40%. Skin involvement (~30-40%) omitted under cap; renal disease less common.
Enzyme deficiency defines osteopetrosis and renal tubular acidosis; cerebral calcification with developmental impairment 30-79%. Dental abnormalities 30-79% omitted under cap.
B-cell lymphoma originating in the spleen, a haematologic organ; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune axis.
Prostate disease lies outside the axes. This umbrella includes noninfectious inflammation and does not establish infection or an autoimmune mechanism.
Rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia; delayed CNS myelination, stage 1 CKD and laryngomalacia each reported in 1/2 patients. Frequencies rest on only two cases.
Benign mesenchymal tumor of pericytic connective and soft tissues; surrounding vessels does not itself establish vascular injury.
Short-rib thoracic skeletal dysplasia; restrictive respiratory insufficiency is a common defining manifestation. Renal and retinal findings are occasional (5-29%).
Nephronophthisis and retinal dystrophy define it; supplied HPO reports developmental delay 80-99% and ovarian endocrine failure 30-79%. Secondary hypertension excluded.
Neoplasm originating in a hair follicle.
Congenital deficiency of the proximal femur with common hip and knee movement limitations.
Immune-mediated localized skin sclerosis; deep muscle, joint or bone involvement causing contracture or growth impairment occurs in about 30-50%. CNS involvement is a minority.
Facial hemangiomas, arterial/cardiac anomalies and brain malformations define it; damaging ocular anomalies are major criteria, with several HPO findings at 30-79%.
Inherited hyaluronan metabolism defect; supplied information does not establish common direct damage to another organ.
Disease of ocular adnexa, including eyelids, lacrimal structures and other tissues supporting the eye.
